About Event

This event is sponsored by Meta, Qualcomm, GitHub, Open Intelligence Foundation, and the PyTorch Foundation.
Join developers, researchers, and builders for the upcoming ExecuTorch Hackathon on October 17 -18 at Founder’s Inc., officially part of Open Source AI Week 2026 .
Hosted in collaboration with Qualcomm , Meta , GitHub , the PyTorch Foundation , and Open Intelligence Foundation , this hands-on event will challenge teams to build innovative AI experiences powered by ExecuTorch —an open-source framework for deploying and running PyTorch models efficiently on edge and on-device hardware.
Participants will work in teams of 3–5 people and select one of three tracks outlined below. Each team will receive a device from their selected track to use during the event.
Compute Track
Build AI applications optimized for the Copilot+ PC powered by Snapdragon® X Elite processors, exploring the potential of powerful, efficient on-device AI computing.
Mobile + XR Track
Create AI-powered experiences for the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra powered by Snapdragon 8 Elite and Samsung Galaxy XR powered by Snapdragon® XR2+ Gen 2 processor, with a focus on mobile intelligence, immersive interaction, and multimodal applications.
IoT Track
Develop intelligent edge and embedded applications using the Arduino ® VENTUNO™ Q boards , combining on-device AI with real-time sensing, control, and connected experiences.
To participate, interested teams must select a track, form a team of 3–5, and submit a project proposal by October 4. Selected teams will be announced by October 7.
Prizes
The top team in each track will receive a prize package for every member of the team: Meta AI glasses and an Arduino® UNO™ Q. Build a standout project, demonstrate the potential of on-device AI, and take home hardware to continue exploring the edge.
Whether you are an experienced edge AI developer or eager to explore the future of open-source, on-device intelligence, the ExecuTorch Hackathon is an opportunity to collaborate, experiment, and build with the latest hardware and software across compute, mobile, XR, and IoT.
Questions? Join our Discord!
Ask questions about the event, connect with other participants, form a team, receive event announcements, and stay up to date throughout the hackathon.
👉 Join here: Join Discord Server
Bring your ideas. Build with ExecuTorch. Help shape the future of open-source, on device AI.

About Open Intelligence Foundation
The Open Intelligence Foundation is a community-first nonprofit founded to protect, strengthen, and advance open-source AI, open models, and open science. Supported by a large community of volunteers and organizations, it takes a bottom-up approach to collaboration, working with academia and researchers to support research, development, and education in open-source AI. The foundation also leads Open Source AI Week , a community-run initiative celebrating open-source AI.
About Founders, Inc.
Founders, Inc. backs early-stage founders in emerging tech with first checks and 55,000 sq. ft. of lab space in San Francisco's Fort Mason. They run year-round programs to help ambitious builders to go from early stage to scalable companies.

Healthcare AI Hackathon
Join OpenAI, AWS, JPM, Troutman Pepper, Pear VC, NEA, and Cathay Innovation for a one-day healthcare AI hackathon bringing together engineers, clinicians, researchers, designers, and founders to build products that solve real problems across health.
Why Attend?
🏆 Compete for up to $5,000 in first/second/third place cash prizes, advisory meetings with leading healthcare AI operators and industry sponsors, and 1:1 pitch opportunities with PearX, NEA, and Cathay

🚀 Connect with leaders from OpenAI, AWS, Stanford Medicine, J.P. Morgan, and leading VC-backed healthcare startups

🤝 Meet investors, founders, and operators shaping the future of healthcare

🏥 Collaborate with clinicians, engineers, researchers, designers, and entrepreneurs

💡 Build something with real-world healthcare impact

🌟 Demo your project to an audience of industry leaders and innovators

Food and drinks will be available

Presented by Pear VC · NEA · Cathay Innovation
Powered by OpenAI · AWS · J.P. Morgan · Troutman Pepper
Healthcare is the largest industry in the world, yet much of its infrastructure still runs on fragmented software, manual workflows, and administrative overhead. Recent advances in foundation models and AI agents have created an opportunity to rethink how healthcare is delivered, from the clinician desktop to the insurance back office to the patient experience.
Life sciences is entering a similar inflection point, as advances in foundation models, biological data, and increasingly automated experimentation begin to reshape how we understand and engineer biology. From target discovery and molecular design to clinical development, AI is creating new ways to compress the traditional drug development cycle and build entirely new categories of therapeutics and research tools.
Throughout the day you'll work directly with venture investors, startup founders, physicians, and operators who spend every day building healthcare companies.
Teams will leave with relationships, recruiting opportunities, and potentially the foundation for their next startup.
Whether you're already building in healthcare or just discovering the space, you'll spend the day working on problems that matter.
What Should You Build?
Build something that meaningfully improves health.
We're less interested in incremental AI wrappers and more interested in products that unlock new capabilities, create new business models, or solve long-standing problems across the healthcare and life sciences ecosystem.
Some areas we're especially excited about include:
🧬 Care Delivery & Clinical Innovation
Build AI that makes care more accessible, personalized, and effective , from diagnostics and specialty care to home-based care, clinical trials, robotics, and entirely new models of care delivery.

🏥 Healthcare Infrastructure & Financing
Build AI that fixes the systems behind healthcare , improving how care is financed, administered, coordinated, and delivered across providers, payers, employers, marketplaces, and supply chains.

🔬 AI × Life Sciences
Build AI that better predicts what will actually happen in biology , using richer, multi-compartment data to model real-world outcomes such as toxicity, delivery, efficacy, and clinical trial endpoints rather than focusing only on molecular binding.

These are examples, not constraints. If you have a compelling idea that improves healthcare, feel free to build it because we want to see it!

You bring the idea. Build the AI that makes it happen.
The Challenge
Build Your AI Co-Founder is a hackathon where you build and ship a company with a founding team of 2–4 co-founders , combining humans and AI.
Every team must have at least one human and one AI co-founder . You decide the rest—including who takes which role, what you build, and how your founding team works together .
AI co-founders can take any role: CEO, CTO, Product, Marketing, Sales, Research, or anything your company needs.
The goal is to experience what it means to build a real company with AI as part of the founding team —from idea to execution to a shipped product.

Build the Product challenge using Emergent
Using Emergent , build and ship a functional app or MVP for a real-world problem. Your product should be something real people can use and should demonstrate how your human–AI founding team turns an idea into a working company.
The focus is on execution : build a useful product, validate it with real users, and show what your AI co-founder contributed to the journey from idea to launch.
Optional Tracks
Build It: Launch the Business
Turn your idea into a launch-ready business. Your AI co-founder helps with research, permits, costs, suppliers, branding, operations, and the launch plan.
Fund It: Raise Capital
Prepare your company to raise funding. Your AI co-founder researches investors, finds the right fit, builds fundraising materials, and helps manage outreach.
Sell It: Get Customers
Get your first customers. Your AI co-founder identifies prospects, researches them, creates personalized outreach, and supports the sales process.
Grow It: Acquire Users
Build a repeatable growth engine. Your AI co-founder helps define your audience, develop positioning, test channels, run experiments, and measure results.
Make It: Build the Product
Turn an idea or problem into a working product. Your AI co-founder helps validate the problem, define the MVP, design the experience, build, test, and iterate.
Run It: Operate the Business
Make your business run better. Your AI co-founder helps improve processes across scheduling, customers, team coordination, reporting, inventory, and automation.
Choose your own
How It Comes Together
The company is up to you. The co-founders are up to you. The roles are up to you. The track defines what you want to accomplish. For example:
Company is AI bookkeeping platform. Co -founders are Human CEO + Human CTO + AI Product + AI Sales
Track is Sell It. Build the product, find potential customers, run outreach, and aim to secure the first paying customers.
Company is AI travel startup. Co -founders are Human Product Lead + AI CEO + AI Growth. Track is Grow It. Build the product, define the target audience, launch growth experiments, and acquire the first users.
Company is Developer productivity tool. Co -founders are Human CTO + AI Product + AI Marketing. Track is Make It. Validate the problem, build the MVP, test it with developers, and ship a working product.
Choose your company. Build your founding team. Pick your mission. Then go build.

Smells like a hackathon. Runs like a pressure test, on you, not just your idea.
Proving Ground runs a three-day Sprint where judges push past the pitch. No script survives real questions about what you tried, what broke, and what you changed.

What this is
A hackathon judges what you built by the end. We watch during the process and look past the end to what may come next.

The team is almost everything. How you make decisions under pressure, how you handle a setback, how you treat each other when something breaks. You'll document that as you go. What we ask you to show and how we question it are built around behavior, not performance.
How it works
Over three days, founders build under real constraint. No script, no rehearsed demo. Judges probe what you tried, what broke, and what you changed, and compare where you started to where you ended.

Discovery Track. Pre-market, no active customer contact yet. For the startup curious, including enterprise folks seriously exploring a leap.
Pre-seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what's changed, pressure-test your next move.

Select teams get invited into the Street Test: 30 days back in the real world, no artificial deadline, no audience. This is where we see if momentum was real or borrowed from the room. It's the part a hackathon can't offer, because a hackathon ends when the weekend does.

The Lowdown 👋
One year ago, we opened a hub where AI builders could show up for each other. On September 22, we're celebrating everyone who did — and everything that got built because of it!
Join us for a night of real conversations about AI, community, and what comes next. We will have:
A panel with AI builders, community leaders, and founders moderated by Jeremiah Owyang

Builders who came here for a hackathon weekend and are still shipping

Stories from startups who built their companies right inside these walls

Plus food, music, a photo booth, community trading cards, and more!

The SVAI Hub was built on one conviction: the best AI doesn't get built in isolation. It gets built by communities — developers leveling up together, founders stress-testing ideas with peers, researchers colliding with practitioners in the same room. In September 2025, we opened our space in the heart of Silicon Valley. Not for vendor pitches. Not for product demos. For the conversations and connections that actually move the field forward.
One year in, the numbers tell part of the story:
100+ AI community events

10,000+ developers, founders, and executives through our doors

6 hackathons that launched real projects and real careers

The numbers tell part of the story. The conversations tell the rest.
Come for the milestone. Stay for the momentum, connections and networking!
Registration requires approval and space is limited. If this sounds like your room, request your spot now!
The Humans at the Mic 🎤
Built Here. Still Building. — Hackathon Winners Spotlight
Victoria Duan — OrchestrAI | Llama Lounge Hackathon, 1st Place
Victoria built the core agentic framework for OrchestrAI, took first place, and hasn't stopped building since — she's now deep in AI developer tooling and exploring how AI changes the way software gets made.

Abraham Bhatti , Rishit Sai & Yash Sanghvi — ToolForge | Llama Lounge Hackathon, 2nd Place
They built an AI agent that creates its own tools, won together, kept competing together, and are now in early customer discovery to turn it into a real product.

Panel: Build Together — The Advantage of Community in AI
Jeremiah Owyang (moderator) — VC at Blitzscaling Ventures, global keynote speaker, and founder of Llama Lounge — the Bay Area's most popular AI startup event series, drawing hundreds of founders, investors, and builders every month.

Grace Gong — Founder of Smart Venture Media, host of two top-ranked VC podcasts (Smart Venture Podcast and Venture with Grace), angel investor, and founder of Smart AI Summits — a LinkedIn Top Voice in Finance with a front-row seat to where AI and venture capital intersect.

Swagata Ashwani — AI Tech Lead & Manager at Boomi, co-lead of the Women in Data SF chapter, and a LinkedIn Top Voice in AI — a technical builder who brings a practitioner's view of how community helps people stay sharp, learn faster, and grow with AI.

Sheena Tu — Co-founder of TechEquity Ai, a Silicon Valley nonprofit that has built a community of 10K+ subscribers and 5K+ annual attendees through forums, workshops, and an annual Summit dedicated to making AI accessible to everyone.

Startup Showcase — Stories from the Hub
Every week, a group of startup founders work from the SVAI Hub. Two of those companies will share what they're building, how this community changed how they built it, and where they are now — in three minutes, no pitch deck.
Evan Powell — Co-founder and CEO, DeepTempo
Evan co-founded StackStorm and helped pioneer event-driven automation before SOAR was a category. Now at DeepTempo, he's building the first transformer-based log language models trained on large-scale network telemetry — models that adapt to polymorphic threats in real time and give security teams behavioral context instead of alert noise. His thesis: the future of security looks like data engineering, and the tools should finally match.

Ivan Lee — Founder and CEO, Datasaur
Ivan sold his first startup to Yahoo, built AI systems at Apple, and has spent the last seven years focused on the problem most AI vendors don't want to talk about: what happens to your data after you hand it over. At Datasaur, he helps enterprises in financial services, healthcare, legal, and government deploy fully air-gapped private LLMs — frontier-model capability, zero data leaving the building. His version of the future: the most powerful AI is the one you fully control.

One year ago, we opened a hub where AI builders could show up for each other. On September 22, we're celebrating everyone who did — and everything that got built because of it!

It gets built by communities — developers leveling up together, founders stress-testing ideas with peers, researchers colliding with practitioners in the same room. 100+ AI community events
10,000+ developers, founders, and executives through our doors
6 hackathons that launched real projects and real careers
